title: Vance in Texas, 9 days of posts

clusters.event: Vance rallies for Paxton in Tyler
clusters.text: JD Vance told a man at a Texas rally who said he loved him that he is the vice president, not James Talarico.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Several outlets report that Vance said this at an Oct. 13, 2026 campaign rally in Tyler, Texas. CBS Austin reports that 
a man in the audience yelled "I love you," and Vance replied, "I love you too, sir... I'm the vice president, not James Talarico."
 The Advocate and the Washington Blade both cite C-SPAN video of the exchange. The Washington Blade says the rally was 
part of Vance's campaigning for Ken Paxton
. The quote, the setting (Texas rally) and the attribution all match the claim as worded. Vance also added "in a totally platonic way," and critics read the remark as a joke about Talarico's sexuality. The claim leaves out that context, but nothing it says is wrong.

clusters.event: Vance rallies for Paxton in Tyler
clusters.text: JD Vance announced that the Trump administration is using the Defense Production Act to expand a key refinery in Tyler, Texas.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Several outlets report that Vance made this announcement at a Tyler, Texas campaign rally for Ken Paxton on Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026. The Tyler Morning Telegraph and Reuters-based coverage quote him saying 
the Trump administration, working with the refinery at Delek, "has used the Defense Production Act and we are gonna expand the refinery right here in Tyler, Texas."
 The Washington Examiner also 
reports that he announced Trump is invoking the Defense Production Act to expand the Delek refinery in Tyler
. This matches the claim's wording. Reporting does note that 
he gave no cost or planned capacity increase
, and that the details of the DPA use have not been fully disclosed. That is a caveat about missing detail and does not contradict the claim, which only says Vance announced it. I did not find a primary document such as a DPA order or a White House release.

clusters.text: James Talarico said that racism is a virus white people spread simply by virtue of their skin color.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Talarico did tweet this on May 8, 2020, after Ahmaud Arbery's death. 
He wrote that "White skin gives me and every white American immunity from the virus," but that "we spread it wherever we go—through our words, our actions, and our systems." He added that "we don't have to be showing symptoms—like a white hood or a Confederate flag—to be contagious."
 (Fox News; Daily Caller; Headline USA). 
Fox News reports he defended the tweets at SXSW, saying they were taken out of context.
 The "virus" metaphor and the attribution to white Americans are accurate. But in the text he quoted, skin color is what makes white people immune to the harm. He said the spreading happens through words, actions and systems, so "simply by virtue of their skin color" is the claim's own gloss. It is a hostile reading of the tweet, not what the tweet says. I found no record of him saying racism spreads merely because of skin color. I also found no connection to Vance in these results, and the tweet was published by Talarico himself, so the attribution is not in doubt.

clusters.event: Vance rallies for Paxton in Tyler
clusters.text: JD Vance suggested James Talarico's internet search history is something people would not want to see, and doubled down on it.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Reporting from Forbes, Fox News and others shows Vance made the remark and then repeated it. At a Tuesday (Oct 13, 2026) rally in Tyler, 
he said "You gotta wonder what the internet search history of a man like that looks like," and added that listeners don't want to find out.
 Asked about it by a reporter, 
he said people who say such things "tend to have some unusual search histories," then added "Maybe he doesn't. Just guessing. But I wouldn't want to see it."
 Fox News itself described this as Vance 
"doubling down on his comments about James Talarico's internet search history."
 Forbes says 
he repeated the line later that day.
 The sources differ on the order of the two remarks, but both happened. The claim is accurate as worded. Vance himself conceded he was speculating, and Forbes noted that 
no evidence or credible allegations of misconduct have surfaced against Talarico.
 The claim doesn't say otherwise.

clusters.event: Vance rallies for Paxton in Tyler
clusters.text: JD Vance implied that James Talarico is gay.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The quote is well documented. At the Oct. 13, 2026 Tyler rally, Vance answered a man in the crowd who shouted that he loved him. 
He said, "I love you, too, Sir! In a totally platonic way — to be clear. I'm the vice president, not James Talarico."
 Newsweek's account of the rally includes the same exchange. 
CNN's analysis says Vance "made a joke that implied James Talarico is gay."
 
CNN's Jake Tapper described it as insinuating that Talarico is gay.
 HuffPost, via Yahoo, and the Advocate use the same reading. Vance did not say Talarico is gay, and I found no statement from him or his office explaining what he meant. "Implied" is therefore an interpretation of a joke, but it is how several established outlets characterize it, and the wording is accurate as a description of the remark. 
Tapper also noted a separate line in which Vance referred to Talarico's comments on "trans children" and then mused about his "internet search history."
